observations.subject: Design-source confidence and evidence limits
observations.observed: The DESIGN source explicitly labels motion confidence low, layout and component confidence medium, says dim opacity is estimated, says pressed and disabled button states were not observed, and says every source capture was desktop with no mobile evidence.
observations.inferredPurpose: This bounds which properties are source-derived observations versus defaults or implementation decisions.

observations.subject: Semantic color system
observations.observed: The implementation theme defines green primary, light-gray secondary, brick-red danger, neon-red warning, three charcoal surface levels, slate chrome, mustard CTA, yellow-green cash, yellow value, gold/cyan rarity, tan progress, and pure-black outline tokens matching the DESIGN palette; dim is implemented as black at Transparency 0.65 from the estimated #00000059 source value.
observations.inferredPurpose: The palette separates action meaning, money, rarity, chrome, and depth without shadows or bevel colors.

observations.subject: Typography tiers
observations.observed: FredokaOne Regular is implemented at 52, 36, 26, and 28 pixels for display, heading, body, and label; BuilderSans Medium at 18 pixels is the caption tier. Only the heading token carries an uppercase flag.
observations.inferredPurpose: Large rounded display type creates the loud hierarchy while BuilderSans preserves legibility in small engine-like HUD chrome.

observations.subject: Corners and strokes
observations.observed: The source specifies hard corners for permanent slabs, 6-pixel rounding for price pills, 10-pixel rounding for prompt plates, 3-pixel contextual black text outlines, 2-pixel white slot borders, and 3-pixel selected borders. The theme implements all of these and also defines an unused full-radius token not present in the source front matter.
observations.inferredPurpose: Hard silhouettes and high-contrast outlines replace soft depth; the extra full-radius token appears to be generic implementation inventory rather than used Loud Slab behavior.

observations.subject: Window anatomy
observations.observed: Window renders a full-screen root, optional dim layer, centered PanelGroup, translucent charcoal Panel, a 72-pixel full-width header, left-aligned uppercase title, a 72-by-72 close button docked inside the header's right edge, and a separately padded content region below the header.
observations.inferredPurpose: This directly realizes the source's crate-like slab, flush color band, and integrated close-square anatomy.

observations.subject: Window clipping and local Z order
observations.observed: The dim is at ZIndex 10 and PanelGroup at 11; within the panel, content is ZIndex 1, header 2, title 3, and close button 4. Both Panel and Content set ClipsDescendants true.
observations.inferredPurpose: The explicit local ordering keeps dim behind the slab and header/close chrome above content, while clipping prevents content from escaping the square window.

observations.subject: Dim treatment and world backdrop
observations.observed: Window implements an approximately 35%-opaque black dim as a full-screen TextButton, but the story environment substitutes a flat #6FA8C9 worldBackdrop color for the source's blur/DepthOfField world treatment.
observations.inferredPurpose: The stand-in gives translucent slabs contrast in UI-Labs without reproducing a live blurred 3D world.

observations.subject: Window sizing contract
observations.observed: Window defaults to 0.6 viewport width by 0.75 viewport height, centers by scale and anchor point, and conditionally applies a UISizeConstraint MaxSize supplied by each story.
observations.inferredPurpose: Scale-first sizing adapts to smaller viewports while MaxSize prevents desktop panels from growing beyond intended dimensions.

observations.subject: Window title treatment
observations.observed: Window uppercases every title, uses 36-pixel heading FredokaOne, left-aligns it with 32-pixel inset, truncates at the end, and applies the 3-pixel contextual black outline.
observations.inferredPurpose: The title remains the loudest textual element in the fixed header band while truncation protects the integrated close-button area.

observations.subject: Window entrance and exit
observations.observed: On mount, Window sets UIScale to 0.8 and tweens it to 1 using Back/Out over 0.25 seconds. Closing guards against duplicate requests, tweens scale to 0.9 and panel transparency to 1 using Quad/In over 0.15 seconds, then invokes onClose after scale tween completion.
observations.inferredPurpose: The slower overshoot entrance and faster shrinking fade exit implement the source's low-confidence cartoon-chunky motion preset.

observations.subject: Primary button variants
observations.observed: ButtonPrimary supports primary and buy as green 6-pixel-rounded slabs, secondary as square light gray, and CTA as square mustard with heading typography. Buy conditionally prepends a white '$' glyph; CTA uppercases its label. All rendered labels are white with black contextual strokes and the component adds no shadow or gradient.
observations.inferredPurpose: One component normalizes source-defined behavioral color roles while preserving the special price-sticker and commitment hierarchies.

observations.subject: Button press and disabled behavior
observations.observed: Primary buttons disable Roblox's AutoButtonColor, squash to scale 0.92 on MouseButton1Down, restore on MouseButton1Up or MouseLeave, and invoke onActivated only when not disabled. Disabled buttons use BackgroundTransparency 0.4 and suppress both squash-in and activation.
observations.inferredPurpose: Squash supplies the press affordance without a color-state shift; transparency and event guards introduce a disabled state.

observations.subject: Close and backdrop dismissal
observations.observed: ButtonClose is a 56-pixel square brick-red TextButton with an outlined, TextScaled X and the same 0.92 press squash. Window routes both the close button and, unless dismissible is false, activation of the full-screen dim TextButton through the animated requestClose path.
observations.inferredPurpose: Both explicit close chrome and backdrop activation dismiss a popup while sharing one duplicate-safe exit animation.

observations.subject: SideButton anatomy
observations.observed: SideButton defaults to a 90-by-90 near-black slab at 0.25 transparency with a 2-pixel white border. A fitted icon occupies the upper area and a TextScaled BuilderSans caption is anchored inside the bottom edge; supplied caption text is normalized by uppercasing the first character and lowercasing the remainder.
observations.inferredPurpose: The component implements the source's icon-dominant edge-rail slab with a small embedded label.

observations.subject: SideButton notification badge
observations.observed: When badge is positive, SideButton adds a 26-by-26 brick-red square badge in its top-right corner, caps counts above 99 as '99+', and gives the badge a white border plus outlined caption text. This badge anatomy is not specified in the source side-button token.
observations.inferredPurpose: It exposes pending-count information without adding another HUD element.

observations.subject: ItemCard content hierarchy
observations.observed: ItemCard is a square-cornered near-black 200-by-240 frame with a white border, padded name label at top, centered fitted square art band, uppercase rarity caption near the bottom, and a full-width 44-pixel buy control anchored at the bottom.
observations.inferredPurpose: The vertical hierarchy prioritizes name and art, then rarity, then purchase action in a dense grid cell.

observations.subject: Rarity and legendary emphasis
observations.observed: Rarity changes caption text color only: common green, rare gold, epic cyan, and legendary gold. Legendary or explicitly emphasized cards additionally use the 3-pixel selected outline instead of the normal 2-pixel outline; the panel fill remains surfaceDeep.
observations.inferredPurpose: The implementation preserves text-only rarity color coding but adds border weight to distinguish the top displayed tier.

observations.subject: CurrencyDisplay formatting
observations.observed: CurrencyDisplay has no background plate. It abbreviates values at one decimal as M from 1,000,000 and K from 10,000, renders the amount in 52-pixel yellow-green FredokaOne with a 3-pixel outline, and optionally renders an 18-pixel white BuilderSans caption below with a 2-pixel outline.
observations.inferredPurpose: The naked, oversized colored amount establishes the bottom-left money corner while the smaller caption carries boost context.

observations.subject: HUD composition
observations.observed: The HUD story renders a left rail with Shop, Items, and Settings; a top-right three-row leaderboard; bottom-left cash and boost caption; bottom-right timer; and bottom-center CTA plus ten numbered hotbar slots.
observations.inferredPurpose: It samples the source's dense edge-docked HUD pattern in one screen.

observations.subject: HUD top inset and compact left rail
observations.observed: HUD queries GuiService:GetGuiInset().Y at render time for top-docked content. Its three left-rail buttons are explicitly overridden from the component's 90-by-90 default to 90-by-44 with 4-pixel gaps and top anchoring.
observations.inferredPurpose: The override preserves the 44-pixel generic tap floor and avoids collisions at the documented 667-by-375 landscape viewport.

observations.subject: Leaderboard column sizing
observations.observed: LeaderboardRow subtracts each column's proportional share of the three 8-pixel layout gaps from nominal 0.4/0.2/0.2/0.2 widths. The plate is 260-by-120, right-docked using the live top inset, and holds three rows.
observations.inferredPurpose: The negative offsets make fractions plus inter-column gaps equal the row width and prevent the cash column from overflowing in 720p captures.

observations.subject: HUD bottom collision avoidance
observations.observed: CurrencyDisplay's wrapper is 320-by-74 with line boxes matching the 52- and 18-pixel tokens. HUD bottom-anchors it 94 pixels above the screen bottom, while a 130-pixel bottom-center container holds the 52-pixel CTA and 52-pixel hotbar with an 8-pixel gap.
observations.inferredPurpose: These explicit footprints and offsets keep the cash caption, hotbar, and left rail from overlapping at the story's narrow landscape target.

observations.subject: HUD PLAY commitment action
observations.observed: The HUD adds one mustard CTA labeled PLAY above the hotbar. Its source comment says the taste DESIGN has no dedicated PLAY button and identifies this as the standard showcase's required contextual primary action.
observations.inferredPurpose: The standard showcase requirement is translated into Loud Slab's one-off commitment-button visual language rather than inferred from the taste itself.

observations.subject: Shop screen hierarchy
observations.observed: Shop centers a dimmed Window titled SHOP, keeps a yellow outlined FEATURED heading fixed above the content region, and displays the six standard items as ItemCards beneath it.
observations.inferredPurpose: The fixed heading anchors the section while item details and purchases scroll independently.

observations.subject: Shop dynamic scroll canvas
observations.observed: Shop uses a ScrollingFrame below the fixed heading. A ref-backed effect sets CanvasSize.Y to UIGridLayout.AbsoluteContentSize.Y immediately and on every AbsoluteContentSize change, disconnecting the property listener on cleanup. The scrollbar is 6 pixels, white, and 0.3 transparent.
observations.inferredPurpose: The canvas follows actual grid wrapping so all six items remain reachable as the number of fitting columns changes.

observations.subject: Shop grid and panel breakpoints
observations.observed: Shop uses a 0.65-by-0.8 scale window capped at 832-by-576 and fixed 200-by-240 grid cells with 12-pixel gaps. Its source comments record three columns near the desktop cap and one column at an approximately 433-pixel mobile panel width, rather than enforcing the DESIGN's four-column collection-grid example.
observations.inferredPurpose: Fixed readable cards wrap naturally, trading source-example column count for viewport adaptability.

observations.subject: Dialog composition
observations.observed: Dialog reuses Window with title CONFIRM, dim enabled, and dismissal enabled; its content is a centered vertical list containing a wrapped purchase question and a green buy-variant button with '$ 2,500'.
observations.inferredPurpose: A purchase confirmation uses the same slab anatomy and price-sticker action grammar as the shop.

observations.subject: Dialog content-fit sizing
observations.observed: Dialog uses scale 0.51 by 0.693 capped at 340-by-260. The source comment explicitly budgets the 72-pixel header, 40 pixels of content padding, 60-pixel body, 20-pixel gap, and 52-pixel button after a prior scale-only dialog clipped its text and action at 667-by-375.
observations.inferredPurpose: The cap represents a content-derived preferred size, while scale permits further shrinking only when the viewport is smaller.

observations.subject: Implemented input events
observations.observed: All three button components use mouse-specific down, up, and leave events for squash feedback and Roblox Activated for the action callback. The dim layer is also a TextButton using Activated. No component branches its behavior by input modality.
observations.inferredPurpose: Activated supplies a modality-neutral action event, while visual press feedback is explicitly mouse-event driven.

observations.subject: Asset sourcing and tinting
observations.observed: Theme centralizes three HUD icon IDs and six item image IDs. SideButton always tints its icon white; ItemCard leaves native image color when iconColor is nil, permitting the acorn's source color while callers may tint monochrome item art.
observations.inferredPurpose: Centralized asset slots avoid literal IDs in components while allowing a mix of monochrome HUD glyphs and item artwork.

observations.subject: Embedded responsive verification notes
observations.observed: HUD, Shop, Dialog, and CurrencyDisplay source comments record concrete prior failure modes and numeric remedies: topbar occlusion, left-rail/cash/hotbar overlap, leaderboard overflow, stale shop canvas height, clipped dialog content, and excess CurrencyDisplay wrapper slack.
observations.inferredPurpose: The comments preserve scenario-specific regression context even though they are not executable assertions.

observations.subject: Story catalog and controls
observations.observed: The storybook points at the complete Stories folder. Component stories expose Window title/dim controls, ItemCard name/rarity/price controls, Currency amount/caption controls, SideButton text/badge controls, and ButtonPrimary text/disabled controls; ButtonClose has no controls.
observations.inferredPurpose: These stories permit manual inspection of component variants and selected configurable states.

observations.subject: Primary-button variant showcase
observations.observed: ButtonPrimary.story displays primary Confirm, secondary Regenerate, buy $150, and CTA REBIRTH NOW simultaneously; one Disabled control is passed to every variant.
observations.inferredPurpose: A single manual story compares the component's four semantic variants and their shared disabled treatment.

observations.subject: Leaderboard typography inconsistency
observations.observed: LeaderboardRow gives Player a 2-pixel black contextual stroke, but Steals, Rebirths, and Cash labels contain no UIStroke children; the three numeric columns still use BuilderSans and semantic yellow, white, and yellow-green colors respectively.

observations.subject: Motion tokens beyond current use
observations.observed: Theme implements instant, fast, normal, and slow durations plus pop, settle, exit, and bounce easings. Current components consume pop/exit for windows and settle for button squash; no inspected story or component invokes the bounce easing.
observations.inferredPurpose: Bounce remains reserved for reward moments described by the source rather than being applied generically.

observations.subject: Window versus screen scrolling responsibility
observations.observed: Window's generic Content is a clipped Frame and does not itself scroll. Shop supplies the only ScrollingFrame in the inspected implementation as a child of Window.
observations.inferredPurpose: The reusable window owns containment while screens opt into scrolling according to their content length.

absences.subject: Right-edge HUD rail
absences.evidence: The source requires a shorter mirrored right rail at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:283-289 and 390-397, but the exhaustive HUD root children are LeftRail, Leaderboard, CashCorner, TimerBadge, and BottomCenter in e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/HUD.story.luau:151-336; no RightRail is constructed.

absences.subject: Toggle and settings-row implementation
absences.evidence: Toggle and toggle-selected are defined at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:118-125 and described at 363-367, while Theme only retains toggleOff at e2e/loud-slab/src/Theme.luau:81-87; none of the six component files or nine story constructions in filesInspected defines or renders a toggle/settings row.

absences.subject: Progress bar, collection search, detached tier filters, and collection index screen
absences.evidence: The source specifies these at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:135-150 and 401-405. The storybook exposes only the inspected Stories root at e2e/loud-slab/src/LoudSlab.storybook.luau:1-5, and no inspected story implements a collection/index screen.

absences.subject: Prompt pills, promotional banners, toasts, and world-space signage
absences.evidence: These source patterns are described at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:151-166 and 398-406. No corresponding component or story appears in the complete filesInspected inventory; HUD's entire constructed child set is visible at e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/HUD.story.luau:151-336.

absences.subject: Actual world blur or DepthOfField
absences.evidence: The source requires blur plus dim at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:297-303. Theme explicitly calls its flat worldBackdrop a story-only stand-in at e2e/loud-slab/src/Theme.luau:88-92, and Window implements only the black dim at e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/Window.luau:91-105.

absences.subject: ScreenGui DisplayOrder bands and ZIndexBehavior Sibling
absences.evidence: The source prescribes ScreenGui ZIndexBehavior and DisplayOrder bands at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:306-309. Window and HUD roots are Frames with local ZIndex/clipping at e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/Window.luau:88-127 and e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/HUD.story.luau:151-156; no inspected target file constructs a ScreenGui or sets either property.

absences.subject: Reduced-motion adaptation
absences.evidence: The source asks for pops to collapse to fades under reduced motion at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:322-331. Window unconditionally starts its scale pop in e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/Window.luau:51-59, and the button components unconditionally define squash tweens at e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/ButtonPrimary.luau:30-39, e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/ButtonClose.luau:12-21, and e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/SideButton.luau:16-25.

absences.subject: Keyboard/gamepad focus, selection, and hover state
absences.evidence: Implemented events are mouse down/up/leave plus Activated at e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/ButtonPrimary.luau:63-83, e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/ButtonClose.luau:38-58, and e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/SideButton.luau:48-67. No inspected component sets selection/focus navigation or distinct keyboard/gamepad/hover visuals.

absences.subject: Selected hotbar slot
absences.evidence: The source says a selected slot gains the 3-pixel selected outline at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:383-385. HotbarSlot always uses slotOutline and has no selected prop at e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/HUD.story.luau:29-54; all ten calls supply only slotNumber/layoutOrder at 319-329.

absences.subject: Currency rate line
absences.evidence: CurrencyDisplay's header comment says an optional rate prop renders an accent-value line at e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/CurrencyDisplay.luau:7-10, but the complete returned children at 40-70 contain only Amount and optional Caption and never read props.rate.

absences.subject: Event-themed header story
absences.evidence: Window supports props.chromeColor at e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/Window.luau:130-134, reflecting event retheming from design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:242-246, but none of Window.story, Shop.story, or Dialog.story passes chromeColor at e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/Window.story.luau:20-25, e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/Shop.story.luau:69-83, or e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/Dialog.story.luau:27-52.

absences.subject: Sold-out, warning, and toggle-state showcases
absences.evidence: The source reports sold-out and toggle states observed while pressed/disabled states were not observed at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:216-219. The inspected stories showcase button Disabled instead at e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/ButtonPrimary.story.luau:13-56; no story renders sold-out warning text or toggle On/Off.

absences.subject: Executable verification assertions
absences.evidence: The target contains story and implementation files only as enumerated in filesInspected. Responsive evidence is preserved as comments, not assertions, for example e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/HUD.story.luau:136-171, e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/Shop.story.luau:34-47, and e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/Dialog.story.luau:27-49.

absences.subject: Full-pill or circular rendered shapes
absences.evidence: The source says there are no circles or full-pill shapes at design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:313-320. Theme defines rounded.full at e2e/loud-slab/src/Theme.luau:58-63, but no inspected component references it; rendered permanent components use none and buy/primary use sm at e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/ButtonPrimary.luau:21-28.

uncertainties: The DESIGN source itself declares motion low-confidence and defaulted because no video existed (design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:322-331); implemented timing correctness cannot be treated as observed source behavior.

The source has no mobile captures and calls mobile composition a declared gap (design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:404-406). The 667-by-375 accommodations in HUD, Shop, and Dialog are implementation adaptations, not validation against source mobile UI.

Comments state that several layouts were measured or verified in-engine (e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/CurrencyDisplay.luau:29-38; e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/HUD.story.luau:136-171; e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/Shop.story.luau:34-47), but this read-only record contains no executable assertions or captured render evidence with which to independently confirm those claims.

The source explicitly leaves disabled button state undefined (design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:216-219), so the implementation's 0.4 background transparency and event suppression (e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/ButtonPrimary.luau:41-83) are not source-validated.

The meaning of the implementation's legendary 3-pixel outline is not fully determined: the source defines selected-outline generally and insists rarity recolors text rather than panels (design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:59-60 and 259-263), while ItemCard applies the outline based on legendary rarity (e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/ItemCard.luau:31-45).

Theme asset comments document Creator Store provenance and intended subjects (e2e/loud-slab/src/Theme.luau:95-137), but code inspection alone cannot verify the assets' current visual appearance, moderation status, or runtime availability.

The CurrencyDisplay comment promises a rate prop but the implementation does not read it (e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/CurrencyDisplay.luau:7-10 and 27-71); it is unclear whether the comment is stale or the rate behavior is incomplete.
The target does not include the mount harness, so ScreenGui-level inset, DisplayOrder, ZIndexBehavior, and input-selection behavior outside these files cannot be determined from the allowed scope.

The source's desktop HUD describes approximately 90-pixel-square rail buttons (design-md/loud-slab/DESIGN.roblox.md:390-397), while HUD.story deliberately uses 90-by-44 at its narrow viewport (e2e/loud-slab/src/Stories/HUD.story.luau:157-197); visual fidelity at the larger reference viewport is not demonstrated by a separate HUD story.

Naming such as 'ButtonPrimary' does not establish semantic equivalence among primary, secondary, buy, and CTA behavior; equivalence here is limited to the directly observed shared implementation in e2e/loud-slab/src/Components/ButtonPrimary.luau:21-140.
